data.tesis_gestora: The Fund follows an active extension strategy on European equities, holding long positions of approximately 130% and short positions of approximately 30% of net assets via derivatives, while maintaining the same overall net market exposure as a traditional long-only portfolio. The investment process is bottom-up, fundamentally driven, supported by quantitative analysis. Goal: maximise alpha generation by buying securities considered attractive and selling short those considered less attractive. In Q1 2026 the Fund outperformed its benchmark MSCI Europe Index (Total Return Net) by 1.78pp (+0.83% vs -0.94%). Key contributors: stock selection and overweight in telecommunication services, and stock selection in materials. Key detractors: underweight in semiconductors & semiconductor equipment and stock selection in transportation. Overweights: energy, banks, telecommunication services. Underweights: capital goods, food/beverage/tobacco, household/personal products. Morningstar Rating: 5 stars; Morningstar Medalist Rating: BRONZE; Category: Europe Large-Cap Blend Equity.
data.decisiones_tomadas: Largest sector increase: semiconductors & semiconductor equipment — ASML topped up following better-than-expected Q4 order numbers as the industry experiences tightness in memory chip supply. Largest sector decrease: pharmaceuticals, biotechnology & life sciences — the Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche Holding was sold from the portfolio as it continues to deliver high-profile trial disappointments and concerns surrounding its high R&D spend in the obesity category persist. Specific stock positioning: maintained underweight in SAP (contributed positively after weak Q4 cloud backlog and Anthropic competition concerns); maintained overweight in SBM Offshore (contributed positively after strong 2025 revenue/EBITDA growth from three new FPSO start-ups); maintained not-holding stance on Eni (detracted after Eni beat expectations); maintained underweight in TotalEnergies (detracted after solid results).
data.contexto_mercado: European markets began Q1 2026 strongly, extending late-2025 momentum on solid growth, upbeat earnings, firmer eurozone PMIs and easing inflation. Sentiment then deteriorated, ending the quarter negatively as tariff uncertainty and conflict between the US and Iran weighed on risk appetite. March's volatility triggered a global sell-off amid higher inflation worries, driven by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to most ships, impacting oil, LNG and fertiliser. Benchmark MSCI Europe TR Net returned -0.94% in the quarter.

citas_textuales.cita: While uncertainty remains over how the Middle East conflict will evolve, our base case scenario assumes near-term de-escalation, as many key players have strong incentives to reduce tensions and avoid further escalation.
In a normalised environment, the outlook for corporate profits is healthy, and revisions are trending higher in most regions and industries.

data.outlook: Base case: near-term de-escalation in Middle East conflict. Healthy corporate profit outlook with positive earnings revisions, supported by fiscal/monetary stimulus and AI investment boom. Eurozone characterised by cautious optimism with activity expected to rise driven by Germany's 2025 fiscal stimulus.

posiciones_destacadas.motivo: Weak Q4 cloud backlog, Anthropic competition. Contributed positively.
Strong 2025 revenue/EBITDA growth, three new FPSOs. Contributed positively.
Detracted — Eni beat expectations (Congo/Angola production, Venezuela cargoes).
Detracted — TotalEnergies beat expectations ($1bn+ oil trading profit, Middle East oil price rally).
Better-than-expected Q4 orders, memory chip supply tightness.
Trial disappointments, high R&D in obesity.
